brief_summary: Vertical three-rung ladder ranking artisan pricing bands from entry-level through grail-tier, each rung annotated with the qualitative description of what distinguishes it, and a bracket marking the entry/low-mid-tier band as the recommended starting zone for a first purchase.
data_sources: artisan-keycaps-buying-guide.mdx § 'What a sane budget looks like' — 'Entry-level artisans are simple single-pour casts — one or two colors, a straightforward shape, no embedded figure — from newer or less oversubscribed makers.'

artisan-keycaps-buying-guide.mdx § 'What a sane budget looks like' — 'Mid-tier covers the bulk of the established maker catalog: multi-part sculpts, embedded foils or figures, hand-painted detailing, from makers with enough of a track record that their raffles draw a real crowd.'

artisan-keycaps-buying-guide.mdx § 'What a sane budget looks like' — 'Grail-tier sits at the top: pieces from a small number of makers whose raffles are reliably oversubscribed, where winning at the original price is rare enough that most of these caps change hands secondhand, at a premium set by scarcity.'

artisan-keycaps-buying-guide.mdx § 'What a sane budget looks like' — 'A newcomer's safest first purchase sits in the entry or low mid-tier band — enough to learn whether the category is worth pursuing before paying a collector's premium for the lesson.'
